title: How the scrolls-* skills work
subtitle: The scrolls-* slash commands create, maintain, move, remove and restore a project's cross-session memory. Pick a command tab to watch what it does, step by step.

nodes.name: /scrolls-setup
nodes.detail: Run once per project. Creates docs/.scrolls/ (or docs/scrolls/ with -u) with the seven memory files, then the SCROLLS.md, CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md pointers. Never overwrites existing scroll files; warns if run from a subdirectory instead of the repo root. No script: it writes files from its templates.

nodes.name: Setup templates
nodes.detail: The single source for every scroll file's starting content and for the SCROLLS_MD / CLAUDE_MD / AGENTS_MD pointer blocks. /scrolls-update reads the pointer blocks from here too, so they are never duplicated.

nodes.name: /scrolls-update
nodes.detail: Run at the end of every session. Reads STARTER.md as the map, cross-checks the conversation against git, then updates each file by its own rule. Also backfills missing SCROLLS.md / CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md pointers (idempotent). If no scrolls exist, it points at /scrolls-setup instead of inventing files.

nodes.name: session_diff script
nodes.detail: Lists uncommitted changes and the commits since docs/.scrolls/ was last touched, with a stat summary. It catches work the conversation forgot (for example after a resume or compaction) without dumping full diffs.

nodes.name: /scrolls-hide
nodes.detail: Renames a visible docs/scrolls/ to hidden docs/.scrolls/ and rewrites the path references inside the scrolls and in SCROLLS.md. -r sweeps a whole tree, such as every package in a monorepo. The opposite of /scrolls-unhide.

nodes.name: /scrolls-unhide
nodes.detail: Renames hidden docs/.scrolls/ to visible docs/scrolls/ and rewrites the path references so nothing breaks. For a new project, /scrolls-setup -u does this in one step.

nodes.name: /scrolls-remove
nodes.detail: The opposite of /scrolls-setup. Deletes the scrolls folder and SCROLLS.md, strips the pointer stubs from CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md (deleting a file only if nothing else is left; -x purges outright), and records it all as ONE commit, maint(memory): scrolls-removed, naming the commit before it. Refuses if anything it would remove has uncommitted changes.

nodes.name: /scrolls-restore
nodes.detail: The counterpart to /scrolls-remove. Finds the newest removal checkpoint (or takes any commit), brings back the scrolls folders and re-inserts the pointer stubs into the files as they are today. Nothing else in the repo is rolled back. --onto mounts the memory on another branch through a temporary worktree.

nodes.name: Git history
nodes.detail: Where /scrolls-remove leaves its checkpoint and /scrolls-restore finds it. /scrolls-update's session_diff also reads it to see what changed since the scrolls were last updated.

nodes.name: /scrolls-help
nodes.detail: Example-driven reference for the whole family: what each command does, the shared -p/-t/-l/-r flags and common recipes. Changes nothing in the repo.

nodes.name: HELP.md / page
nodes.detail: Prints references/HELP.md as chat text, or with -e serves it as a styled page on an OS-assigned localhost port with light/dark and colorize/plain toggles.

nodes.name: New agent session
nodes.detail: A fresh session knows nothing. Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md automatically; other harnesses read AGENTS.md. Both lead to SCROLLS.md and then STARTER.md, so the project's memory is loaded before work starts.

nodes.name: AGENTS.md
nodes.detail: A short stub for non-Claude agent harnesses that points at CLAUDE.md. Other content in the file is left alone.

nodes.name: CLAUDE.md
nodes.detail: A fixed two-line stub near the top: read SCROLLS.md first. Inserted, never overwriting the project's own instructions.

nodes.name: SCROLLS.md
nodes.detail: The one file that knows where the scrolls folder lives (hidden or visible, at any path). /scrolls-hide and /scrolls-unhide rewrite its path.

nodes.name: STARTER.md
nodes.detail: The map of the memory: each scroll, when to read it and how to update it. Projects can add their own scrolls here (architecture, security reviews); /scrolls-update follows each one's documented rule.

nodes.name: HANDOFF.md
nodes.detail: Where things stand right now, what just happened, open threads. Overwritten each session, never appended.

nodes.name: SPEC.md
nodes.detail: Gets a new section only for features that actually shipped, described from the user's side, not the implementation's.

nodes.name: PLAN.md
nodes.detail: The ticket list: flip completed tickets, reprioritize, add newly found work.

nodes.name: GAP_* files
nodes.detail: GAP_ANALYSIS.md lists what isn't done; GAP_CONTEXT.md says why (deliberate cut, oversight, blocker). Closing a gap deletes it from both.

nodes.name: WISDOM.md
nodes.detail: Constraints, traps, ditches and lessons. An entry is added only when the session actually taught something new.

setup.label: /scrolls-setup
setup.summary: Run once per project: creates the memory folder and the pointers that lead every new session to it.

steps.title: Check, then read templates
steps.text: It first checks for an existing scrolls folder. If one has files, it stops and asks: it never overwrites real memory. Then it reads its own templates.

steps.title: Create STARTER.md
steps.text: It creates docs/.scrolls/ (or docs/scrolls/ with -u) and writes STARTER.md: the map listing every scroll and how to update it.

steps.title: Create HANDOFF.md
steps.text: The current-state snapshot: where things stand and what's open.

steps.title: Create SPEC.md
steps.text: What the project does for its users, filled from a quick look at the code.

steps.title: Create PLAN.md
steps.text: The ticket list for what comes next.

steps.title: Create the gap files
steps.text: GAP_ANALYSIS.md (what's missing) and GAP_CONTEXT.md (why), kept as a pair.

steps.title: Create WISDOM.md
steps.text: Constraints, traps and lessons. That makes seven memory files.

steps.title: Write SCROLLS.md
steps.text: A file at the project root that says where the scrolls folder is: docs/.scrolls/STARTER.md.

steps.title: Add a stub to CLAUDE.md
steps.text: A two-line 'read SCROLLS.md first' stub goes at the top. CLAUDE.md is created if missing; existing instructions are kept.

steps.title: Add a stub to AGENTS.md
steps.text: The same idea for Codex and other agent tools: AGENTS.md points at CLAUDE.md. Setup is done.

session.label: New session
session.summary: What a fresh agent session does with the memory: follow the pointers, then read.

steps.title: Claude Code opens CLAUDE.md
steps.text: A new session knows nothing about the project. Claude Code loads CLAUDE.md automatically.

steps.title: Other agents open AGENTS.md
steps.text: Codex and other harnesses read AGENTS.md instead.

steps.title: AGENTS.md → CLAUDE.md
steps.text: …which sends them to CLAUDE.md too, so every agent takes the same path.

steps.title: CLAUDE.md → SCROLLS.md
steps.text: The stub says: read SCROLLS.md first.

steps.title: SCROLLS.md → STARTER.md
steps.text: SCROLLS.md knows the folder's real path: hidden or visible, at the repo root or inside a package.

steps.title: Read HANDOFF.md first
steps.text: STARTER.md says what to read when. HANDOFF.md comes first: current state and open threads.

steps.title: Then PLAN.md
steps.text: What's next to work on.

steps.title: And WISDOM.md
steps.text: The traps not to fall into again. SPEC and the gap files are read when the task touches them.

update.label: /scrolls-update
update.summary: Run at the end of every session: records what happened, each file by its own rule.

steps.title: Look at git
steps.text: The session_diff script lists uncommitted changes and the commits since the scrolls were last touched.

steps.title: Cross-check the session
steps.text: That catches work the conversation forgot, for example after a resume or compaction.

steps.title: Read the map
steps.text: STARTER.md says which scrolls exist and each one's update rule, including any the project added itself.

steps.title: HANDOFF.md: overwrite
steps.text: Replaced with a fresh snapshot. Never appended.

steps.title: SPEC.md: only what shipped
steps.text: A section is added only for features that really work, described for users.

steps.title: PLAN.md: tick and add
steps.text: Done tickets flip [ ] → [x]; newly found work becomes new tickets.

steps.title: Gap files: in lockstep
steps.text: A closed gap is deleted from both files. A new gap gets a line in one and its reason in the other.

steps.title: WISDOM.md: only if new
steps.text: An entry is added only when the session taught something new.

steps.title: Backfill pointers
steps.text: Missing SCROLLS.md, CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md stubs are added. Safe to run every time; nothing is overwritten.

hide.label: /scrolls-hide
hide.summary: Turns a visible docs/scrolls/ into hidden docs/.scrolls/ without breaking anything.

steps.title: Rename the folder
steps.text: docs/scrolls/ becomes docs/.scrolls/. Path references inside the scrolls are rewritten to match.

steps.title: Rewrite SCROLLS.md
steps.text: SCROLLS.md now points at docs/.scrolls/STARTER.md.

steps.title: Chain still works
steps.text: New sessions still find the memory. With -r, every package in a monorepo is done in one run.

unhide.label: /scrolls-unhide
unhide.summary: Turns hidden docs/.scrolls/ into visible docs/scrolls/ without breaking anything.

steps.title: Rename the folder
steps.text: docs/.scrolls/ becomes docs/scrolls/. Path references inside the scrolls are rewritten.

steps.title: Rewrite SCROLLS.md
steps.text: SCROLLS.md now points at docs/scrolls/STARTER.md.

steps.title: Chain still works
steps.text: Nothing else changes. For a new project, /scrolls-setup -u gives a visible folder from the start.

remove.label: /scrolls-remove
remove.summary: The opposite of setup: takes the memory out in one commit that can always be undone.

steps.title: Check for uncommitted work
steps.text: It refuses if anything it would remove has uncommitted changes, because those could not be restored.

steps.title: Delete the scrolls
steps.text: The scrolls folder and SCROLLS.md are deleted.

steps.title: Strip the stubs
steps.text: The pointer stubs come out of CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md. A file is deleted only if nothing else is left (or with -x).

steps.title: One checkpoint commit
steps.text: Everything lands as ONE commit, maint(memory): scrolls-removed, naming the commit before it.

restore.label: /scrolls-restore
restore.summary: The counterpart to remove: brings the memory back from git, and nothing else.

steps.title: Find the checkpoint
steps.text: It finds the newest scrolls-removed commit, or uses any commit you name. --list shows the options.

steps.title: Bring back the scrolls
steps.text: The scrolls folders come back exactly as they were before removal.

steps.title: Re-insert the stubs
steps.text: The pointer stubs go back into CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md as they are today. No other file is rolled back.

steps.title: Record it
steps.text: It is recorded as one commit. --onto puts the memory on another branch through a temporary worktree.

help.label: /scrolls-help
help.summary: A reference for the whole family. It changes nothing in the repo.

steps.title: Show the reference
steps.text: What each command does, the shared -p / -t / -l / -r flags and common recipes, as chat text.

steps.title: Or as a web page
steps.text: With -e / --online it serves the same reference as a styled local page, with light/dark and colour toggles.

footer.label: Simulated
footer.text: Scripted explanation of the scrolls skill family, not measured activity.
footer.note: Shared flags: -p path · -t repo root · -l current dir · -r recurse
